candidates.title: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding
candidates.content: Speculative decoding (SD) accelerates large language model inference by reducing the sequential cost of token-by-token generation. Advanced SD methods reduce proposal cost with parallel drafters that predict entire blocks in one forward pass, but overall speedup still depends on acceptance length. On-policy distillation (OPD) can push well-trained drafters beyond acceptance-length plateaus, yet conventional pipelines collect supervision through sequential draft-and-verify rollouts. Our key insight is that on-policy supervision need not inherit these dependencies: a draft block can be supervised using only its reference prefix and draft-sampled history. We propose SpecOPD, a branch-parallel OPD framework that parallelizes draft sampling and target supervision across independent branches drawn from the evolving drafter policy at reference anchors. We pack these branches into proposal trees to share target-prefix computation, using tree masks for full attention, branch-consistent indexer groups for sparse attention, and indexed state replay for linear attention to preserve each branch's history. candidates.title: VeriSpoof: Beyond Real or Fake with One Audio LLM
candidates.content: A speech deepfake detector estimates whether a recording is synthetic, but a forensic analyst also asks which system produced it, whether recordings share a source, and what evidence supports each conclusion. We present VeriSpoof, an audio language model that unifies five tasks with shared weights: deepfake detection, generator attribution (generator, acoustic model and vocoder), recording-condition analysis, synthesized-span localisation, and source verification. Each decision is supported by grounded rationales whose statements can be independently verified. Answers are scored by sentence likelihood, allowing detection and source verification to be thresholded without separate heads. Rationale statements can be checked against waveform measurements, span labels, or generator metadata. Counterfactual examples train decisions to follow the stated evidence. Across the 14 Speech-DF-Arena test sets, VeriSpoof-Plus achieves 2.14% pooled EER, ranking third of 28 systems and first among open-weight systems. candidates.title: Human-to-Robot Transfer via Bridging Representation and Action Space in VLAs
candidates.content: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies provide a strong starting point for deployment, but adapting them to a target robot and environment still requires costly embodiment-specific demonstrations. Human demonstrations are far easier to collect, yet directly leveraging them is challenging due to the substantial human-robot embodiment gap, particularly when the underlying VLA has been pretrained primarily on robot data. We introduce H2RB (Human-To-Robot Bridge), a human-robot co-training framework for adapting pretrained VLA policies from unpaired human and robot demonstrations. H2RB bridges the embodiment gap at both interfaces: geometry-anchored alignment grounds human and robot observations in a compatible representation, while a decoupled-decoder tokenizer shares action latents without forcing both domains through a single action mapping. This design allows human demonstrations to provide useful behavioral supervision while retaining the rich visual, semantic, and control priors of the pretrained VLA. candidates.title: datasette-apps 0.3a0
candidates.content: Release: datasette-apps 0.3a0 Datasette Apps adds support for hosting and editing custom HTML applications inside of Datasette. These can be created by hand, but it's easier to create them using LLMs via Datasette Agent . This release improves that integration: Apps can now be tagged in Datasette Agent chat messages by typing # , which autocompletes from the apps the user has permission to view. New app_add_stored_queries() and app_remove_stored_queries() tools let the agent manage which stored queries an app is allowed to call. Granting a write query requires approval from the user first. app_create() now checks that each requested stored query exists and that the user can view it, and asks the user to approve any write queries before the app is created. The "View app" buttons shown by the agent tools, and the links on # app references, now open the app full screen in the Datasette Agent panel. Tags: datasette , datasette-agent , datasette-apps

When combined with datasette-apps this means you can prompt a database-backed app into existence and then modify it from the chat that sits next to that app. You can try it by signing in with your GitHub account to agent.datasette.io . candidates.title: Testing the Addition of an Individualized Vaccine to Durvalumab and Tremelimumab and Chemotherapy in Patients With Metastatic Triple Negative Breast Cancer
candidates.content: [PHASE2] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: National Cancer Institute (NCI) | 适应症: Anatomic Stage IV Breast Cancer AJCC v8, Invasive Breast Carcinoma, Metastatic Triple-Negative Breast Carcinoma. This phase II trial studies how well nab-paclitaxel, durvalumab, and tremelimumab with or without personalized synthetic long peptide vaccine (neoantigen vaccine) works in treating patients with triple negative breast cancer that has spread from where it first started (primary site) to other places in the body (metastatic). Chemotherapy drugs, such as nab-paclitaxel, work in different ways to stop the growth of tumor cells, either by killing the cells, by stopping them from dividing, or by stopping them from spreading. Immunotherapy with monoclonal antibodies, such as durvalumab and tremelimumab, may induce changes in body's immune system and may interfere with the ability of tumor cells to grow and spread. Vaccines made from peptides may help the body build an effective immune response to kill tumor cells. It is not yet known whether giving nab-paclitaxel, durvalumab, and tremelimumab with or without neoantigen vaccine will work better in treating patients with triple negative breast cancer.

candidates.title: A Study to Evaluate INT101 in Healthy Adults for the Prevention of Norovirus Gastroenteritis
candidates.content: [PHASE1] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: InThera Inc. Korea | 适应症: Norovirus Infections, Norovirus Gastroenteritis. This study is being conducted to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of INT101, an investigational vaccine intended to prevent norovirus gastroenteritis, in healthy adults. INT101 contains multivalent norovirus antigens (GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17) and is administered as an intramuscular injection. Participants will receive either INT101 or a placebo, given three times at 4-week intervals. This is a single-center, single-blind, randomized, dose-escalation, placebo-controlled, multiple-dose, Phase 1 clinical trial. Approximately 30 healthy adult participants will be enrolled and randomly assigned to receive either a low dose or high dose of INT101, or a matching placebo, in a 2:1 ratio within each dose group. The primary objective is to evaluate the safety of multiple intramuscular doses of INT101 compared to placebo. The secondary objective is to evaluate the immunogenicity (antibody response) of INT101 compared to placebo. Participants will be followed for approximately 6 months after their last dose to monitor safety and immune response.

candidates.title: THE EFFECTS OF HPV VACCİNATİON AND MESSAGE FRAMİNG
candidates.content: [NA] COMPLETED | 申办方/赞助方: Ankara Medipol University | 适应症: Human Papillomavirus Infection, HPV Vaccination, Vaccine Hesitancy. Background: University students are at high risk for HPV infection, while HPV vaccination rates remain low. Message framing strategies may influence vaccination-related perceptions and intentions. Objective: This study aims to compare the effects of gain- and loss-framed HPV vaccination messages on HPV risk perception, HPV knowledge, and vaccination intention among university students. Methods: This randomized controlled experimental study includes university students from the health sciences faculty of a foundation university. Participants are assigned to gain-framed, loss-framed, and control groups. Data are collected using the Human Papillomavirus Knowledge Scale and the HPV Risk Perception Questionnaire. Statistical analyses include one-way ANOVA, two-way ANOVA, and Chi-square tests. The study is designed in accordance with CONSORT 2010 and EQUATOR Network reporting guidelines. Keywords: message framing; gain-loss framing; human papillomavirus; vaccination

candidates.title: DNA mimic helical foldamers with up to 100 units: synthesis and recognition of a multiprotein complex
candidates.content: Abstract DNA mimic foldamers (DMFOs) are helically folded aromatic oligoamides that mimic the shape and charge distribution of double-stranded B-DNA. DMFOs consist of an alternation of two amino acid monomers, M and Q. Here, we introduce a new synthetic approach of (MQ) n oligomers on solid phase that enabled the production of sequences as long as a 100mer, formally equivalent to a 50-base pair DNA duplex. The approach takes advantage of dimeric Fmoc-MQ-OH as building blocks. Three such macromonomers were synthesized using Q and M units bearing different side chains. Solid phase synthesis protocols were validated in all series. Helix handedness was shown to be determined by a single chiral residue. The purified long oligomers were analyzed by reversed phase HPLC, mass spectrometry, circular dichroism, and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for their purity, identity, and helix-handedness bias. Clusters of foldamers forming in the presence of Ca 2+ could be visualized by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM). candidates.title: Detection and quantification of DNA double-strand breaks by genomic and imaging methods: a critical appraisal of capabilities and limitations
candidates.content: Abstract DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are the most genotoxic form of DNA damage. Unrepaired DSBs may cause loss of chromosome fragments at mitosis, while incorrectly repaired DSBs can cause chromosome aberrations and other adverse effects, leading to cell cycle arrest, senescence, cell death, or neoplastic transformation. Detecting and quantifying DSBs is important in studies of genome instability, aging, and cancer. Methods of detecting and quantifying DSBs fall into two broad categories: imaging-based methods, used to detect and localize DNA breaks in individual cells, and genomic methods, a new category utilizing massively parallel DNA sequencing to map DSBs genome-wide in a cell population. Imaging and genomic methods yield fundamentally different information. This review focuses on a critical evaluation of the capabilities and limitations of genomic and imaging methods for the detection and quantification of DSBs. It explains why the class of genomic methods, where quantification is based on counting the detected unique DSBs and the number of cells in the sample, results in inaccurate assessment of the average number of DSBs per cell and how this problem can be solved. candidates.content: Abstract The rise of multidrug-resistant pathogens underscores the need for precise antimicrobial strategies beyond conventional antibiotics. Conjugation-based approaches offer a powerful yet underexploited means of delivering targeted genetic interventions within microbial communities. Here, we combine selective killing modules with optimized conjugative vectors to target antibiotic-resistant pathogens and clinically relevant resistance plasmids. First, we engineered toxin–intein modules, programmable cassettes that restrict toxic activity to specific regulatory contexts. We developed modules targeting Shigella spp., Salmonella enterica , and bacteria carrying the resistance plasmid pOXA-48, demonstrating tunable and selective activity at both species and strain levels. To identify the optimal delivery platform, we compared mobilizable and conjugative plasmids, finding that conjugative systems consistently outperform mobilizable ones by approximately one order of magnitude. candidates.title: Functional analysis of small-molecule and protein binding domains using monomeric streptavidin-based two-component biosensors
candidates.content: Protein biosensors are important analytical and diagnostic tools that convert molecular recognition into measurable activity. Most common two-component biosensors require two non-competing recognition domains, yet binding affinity and specificity alone do not reliably predict their compatibility with the rest of the biosensor. We report a modular platform that exploits monomeric streptavidin (mSA2) as a surrogate recognition domain, enabling rapid functional evaluation of candidate binders in the context of biosensor scaffold without requiring a second ligand-specific binding protein. We established a chromatography-free protocol for recovering functional mSA2-based biosensor components from Escherichia coli. Using biotinylated small molecules methotrexate and vitamin D3, as well as heart failure protein biomarkers galectin-3 and S100A7 we demonstrate ligand-dependent reporter biosensor activation. The developed platform provides a scalable approach for rapid binder evaluation and biosensor prototyping, streamlining biosensor development using binding domains generated by directed evolution or computational protein design.

candidates.title: Developing synthetic auxin-based trans-kingdom signaling
candidates.content: Synthetic trans-kingdom signaling systems with tunable transduction properties provide a unique avenue to explore how communication between organisms coordinate behaviors without the confounding complexity of natural systems. However, existing trans-kingdom signaling systems suffer from either toxic signal molecules, a need for rare precursors for signal generation, or transduction machinery which is either species-specific or cannot be easily tuned. This limits their capacity to be broadly applied across kingdoms and their utility as a model system to study trans-kingdom interactions. In this work we elucidate the design principles for a trans-kingdom signaling system based on the plant phytohormone, Indole 3-Acetic Acid (auxin), that overcomes these challenges. We demonstrate how auxin biosynthesis can be engineered into a model sender organism, the cyanobacteria Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942, and how this signal can be tuned with low leak and high dynamic range. We also show these signals can be connected to gene expression using tunable synthetic auxin-responsive signaling systems across multiple kingdoms. candidates.title: Mapping and Probing the Substrate Scope of a Ketoamide-Forming Splicease by Computational Design
candidates.content: -Keto-{beta}-amide warheads are protease-inhibiting pharmacophores in peptidomimetic antiviral drugs and drug leads, but their diversity-oriented synthesis for library-based drug discovery can be challenging. The same moiety is installed enzymatically in gene-encoded peptides by tyramine spliceases from spliceotide natural products. However, their substrate scope remains poorly understood. We mined bacterial spliceotide pathways for multi-precursor spliceases and identified HypX from Hyella patelloides that modified 5 of 7 native precursors in E. coli. Single-point mutagenesis showed promiscuity for HypX and the previously identified PlpX but different substrate scopes, suggesting that splicease mining can provide enzymes for focused libraries of various substrate types. To evaluate multipoint variants without exhaustive screening, we combined AlphaFold3 models with Rosetta calculations to rank millions of variants. Top-scoring peptides were spliced more efficiently than single-point mutants. Structural modeling rationalized position-specific tolerance, including a cofactor constraint. candidates.title: CFDP1 is required for histone variant H2A.Z deposition by the human SRCAP chromatin remodeling complex
candidates.content: Abstract Craniofacial Developmental Protein 1 (CFDP1) is a member of the evolutionarily conserved family of Bucentaur (BCNT) proteins and is required for cell survival and differentiation during tooth development. Its yeast homolog is involved in histone variant H2A.Z deposition by the yeast SWR1C remodeler. Direct connections between CFDP1, H2A.Z deposition, and the mammalian SWR1 homolog, Snf2-Related CREBBP Activator Protein (SRCAP), are poorly understood. Here, we perform detailed biochemical reconstitution and characterization of the human SRCAP complex (SRCAP-C). We find that CFDP1 weakly interacts with SRCAP-C in a salt concentration-dependent manner and is essential for H2A.Z dimer exchange by SRCAP-C. We show that CFDP1 stimulates the basal ATPase activity of reconstituted SRCAP-C, suggesting a requirement for CFDP1 in regulating intrinsic catalytic ATPase activity. Additionally, CFDP1 deficiency in human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) leads to a genome-wide reduction of H2A.Z, H3K27me3, and H3K4me3 deposition, accompanied by the upregulation of developmental genes normally marked by these modifications. candidates.title: Systematic engineering of synthetic minimal promoters for tunable transgene expression in mammalian cells
candidates.content: Abstract Fine-tuning transgene levels is crucial in fundamental and applied research. Native promoters are broadly utilized to regulate transgene expression. However, their large size and structural complexity hinder predictable tuning, constrain compatibility with viral vectors with limited capacity, and increase the risk of homologous recombination. Synthetic promoters are short de novo sequences, typically consisting of an enhancer region, which is positioned upstream of a minimal promoter that determines transcription initiation efficiency. Enhancer optimization typically yields coarse activation shifts, alters response curves, and requires case-by-case optimization. Synthetic minimal promoter architecture enables fine-tuning that is potentially compatible with any enhancer region. In this study, we systematically optimized minimal promoter sequences, core element composition, and regulatory motif sequences. Our findings support a modular model of minimal promoter function in which cis- regulatory elements from different minimal promoters can be mixed, altered, added, or deleted to yield predictable expression outcomes. candidates.title: More is more: why cell number matters in microscopy
candidates.content: Nature Methods, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03297-2 We argue that cell number must be treated as a core experimental parameter to elevate microscopy beyond simple trend detection towards robust quantitative measurements capable of revealing the full complexity of biological systems. We demonstrate that, while central tendencies are readily captured, resolving a distribution’s underlying shape and its rare events necessitates a hundredfold increase in cell number, often rendering high magnification microscopy statistically underpowered.

candidates.title: AdSteer: Native Advertising in Large Language Model Generation
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.04147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) services face rapidly rising serving costs. To sustain free or affordable access for a broad user base, alternative monetization mechanisms are needed. Native advertising offers a promising approach, as it creates economic value by aligning user intent with merchant offerings. Yet how to integrate sponsored content naturally into LLM responses remains largely underexplored. Existing approaches primarily rely on prompt-level injection, multi-pass rewriting, or fine-tuning, which can compromise response quality or introduce additional computational costs. We propose AdSteer, a lightweight decoding-time advertising framework that adaptively adjusts token probabilities to integrate contextually appropriate advertisement into responses. AdSteer calibrates the strength and duration of advertising influence, making sponsored content a natural part of the response. Experiments on GEM-Bench across three application scenarios show that AdSteer achieves an average improvement of 14.1% in overall score over the strongest baselines and 22.5% fewer total tokens on average than rewrite-based methods. candidates.title: Alignment Faking Depends on the Value, Not Just the Model
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.03650v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language models can follow a directive when they believe they are monitored and abandon it when they believe they are not, a pattern termed Alignment Faking. Prior work establishes this for harmful-content objectives and a handful of moral-foundations values, leaving open how it distributes across a wider value space. We argue it is value-dependent: whether compliance survives a change in perceived oversight is a property of the model--value pairing, not of the model alone. Our framework profiles Alignment Faking per value, scoring each model-value pair under three conditions: bare (no system prompt), unmonitored, and monitored. On 32 ValueBench dimensions across ten open- and closed-weight models (8B-~675B), compliance gaps span 0.05-0.50, with a distilled 70B above a ~675B model. We observe that majority of the structural variance depends on which model was asked about which value and not on the model or value alone. A six-category taxonomy over reasoning traces tracks the behavioural shift: training-signal reasoning dominates under monitoring and value-conflict reasoning dominates when unmonitored. candidates.title: The \`{I}r\`{o}y\`{i}nSpeech Text Corpus: 24,905 Curated Yor\`ub\'a Sentences for Speech and Language Technology
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.05366v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: \`{I}r\`{o}y\`{i}nSpeech is a 42-hour, 80-speaker Yor\`ub\'a read-speech corpus whose audio has been distributed by ELRA since 2024. This paper describes the release of its text component: 24,905 unique, hand-verified, tone-marked Yor\`ub\'a sentences (275,897 tokens; 15,687 types), curated in 2022 as recording prompts. Roughly 11,000 sentences were adapted from openly licensed news material; the remainder were written in-house to broaden coverage beyond the religious translation that dominates existing Yor\`ub\'a corpora. Every sentence was checked by hand for tone-mark accuracy, edited for read-aloud clarity and a neutral register, and localised so that non-Yor\`ub\'a personal and place names appear in Yor\`ub\'a form. Preparing the text for release surfaced systematic Unicode normalisation failures affecting more than 60% of lines (with precomposed and decomposed forms of the same letter co-occurring within single sentences) which we document and correct. candidates.title: CogniLife: Continuous Cognitive Distillation for Deployed Multi-Expert Agent Marketplaces
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.04483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-expert agent marketplaces -- where creators publish domain-specific AI experts for end users to consult -- are an emerging deployment pattern for language technology. A published expert can receive many requests yet little evidence about its creator, who remains active elsewhere: the cold-expert problem. We frame continuous cognitive distillation as converting attributed creator observations into revisable decision rules, communication patterns, and domain procedures. CogniLife proposes a cross-expert attribution design for this problem, with Creator Profiles for transferable creator patterns and Expert Journals for listing-specific knowledge; this design is not yet implemented or evaluated. A deployed platform partially realizes the surrounding lifecycle through creator-authorized authoring, capability-owned proposal filtering, and reversible consolidation of eligible owner-scoped memory. candidates.title: Reconstructing Fraudulent Strategies in Online Payments via Interpretable Inverse Reinforcement Learning
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.04819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Payment fraud causes financial losses and undermines users' trust in web payment services. Although fraud detection is a critical defense for payment security, complex and diverse fraudulent behaviors can still evade detection. Generating fraud samples for data augmentation can broaden detectors' coverage of different fraud patterns. However, existing methods matching the distribution of transaction attributes alone do not ensure that generated sequences preserve the sequential relationships among transaction choices, payment feedback, and subsequent behavioral adjustments. To this end, we propose PaySeqGen, an interpretable inverse reinforcement learning framework that reconstructs fraud behavior policies from fraudsters' observed payment trajectories. We design a mechanism for constructing candidate actions to support plausible payment sequence generation while enabling exploration. The framework also learns interpretable behavioral rewards that capture fraudsters' preferences across different transaction contexts. candidates.title: The Web Doesn't Sit Still: Adversarial Self-Evolving Attacks on Search Agents
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.03754v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise for empowering search agents to tackle complex information-seeking tasks. However, since acquiring external information necessitates web search, these agents are highly susceptible to various adversarial attacks (e.g., malicious information injection or stealthy context manipulation). Existing attack strategies inevitably rely on static and human-crafted templates, failing to emulate the dynamic and complex nature of real-world threats. In this paper, we propose an adversarial self-evolution framework that integrates bi-level optimization between the attacker's strategy evolution and the defender's adaptive mitigation, to expose the vulnerabilities of search agents. Specifically, we introduce the Contrastive Rollout Evolutionary Optimization (CREO) method to drive the directional evolution of the attack strategy population via contrastive evolutionary signals. To provide a stable environment for this continuous evolution, we further construct a controlled sandbox and design fine-grained metrics to quantify internal vulnerabilities. candidates.title: Budgeted Task-Aware Acquisition of Dynamic Networks
candidates.content: arXiv:2609.05862v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Learning on dynamic graphs is difficult when changes in the underlying network are only partially observed. Acquiring current graph information incurs observation and computational costs, making complete updates impractical under limited resources. This paper focuses on budgeted task-aware acquisition on dynamic networks, where a model needs to decide which stale graph information to refresh for a downstream task. We propose Scout, a lightweight framework that learns the task value of querying each node from the maintained graph and observation history. Our evaluation covers one synthetic and 4 real-world dynamic networks, 2 downstream tasks, 9 acquisition baselines, and several query budgets. Scout achieves the highest mean downstream performance in 15 of the 21 benchmark-budget settings and ranks within the top two in 19 of them. Its average rank is 1.4, compared with 3.2 for the strongest baseline. On the same dynamic network, task-matched acquisition improves link-prediction AUC by 0.005-0.007 and node-classification accuracy by 0.007-0.017 over task-mismatched acquisition. candidates.title: Beyond Unit-Circle Eigenvalues: Invariant Bases for Stable State Space Dynamics
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.02174v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Diagonal state space models process long sequences at linear cost, yet the same transition is applied at every step of a rollout, so an unconstrained recurrence holds no quantity fixed and the state decays or grows without bound. Current designs constrain one quantity, and preserving one does not guarantee preservation of the others, so a model can hold its norm to machine precision while momentum drifts by hundreds of percent. We claim that the conserved quantities of a diagonal recurrence are layered, that each layer requires a strictly stronger condition on the operator, and that a unit-modulus spectrum reaches only the outermost. Acting on the claim, we enforce the conditions required for every layer by construction. The generator of the Kronecker-Cayley transition (KC) is a graph Laplacian over object subspaces, $\mathbf{H}=\mathbf{L}\otimes I_m$, advanced by a Cayley transform, and the step stays diagonal at $O(N^3+N^2m)$ cost.
